Gaps: no chatbot or voicebot shipped as such, pgvector and LlamaIndex not in the profile, no health-insurance domain. Essen is one of the listed locations and you live there.

form_fields.label: Why BITMARCK?
form_fields.value: You build the software most statutory health insurers run on; a chatbot there must be correct and careful with data, which is the kind of reliability work I have done.

form_fields.label: Salary expectation
form_fields.value: €70,000 gross/year (range €60,000–75,000). Must be above the EU Blue Card threshold.

form_fields.label: Location
form_fields.value: Essen; open to other BITMARCK locations.

questions.q: How would you build a RAG chatbot for a health insurer?
questions.a: Retrieval over approved documents only, citations in every answer, evaluation set with domain experts (RAGAS + ground truth, as in your thesis), fallback to a human, no personal data in prompts or logs, monitoring of answer quality. Evidence: PrismaChat evaluation, Kniit ground-truth loop (33/45 → 93/90).

questions.q: Which vector database would you choose, Qdrant or pgvector?
questions.a: You used Qdrant, Pinecone and Azure AI Search; pgvector keeps vectors next to relational data in Postgres (simpler ops), Qdrant scales better for large collections and filtering. Be honest that you haven't used pgvector.

questions.q: Tell us about integrating an LLM into a backend and frontend.
questions.a: Covestro: LangGraph agent + FastAPI + React, Docker, AWS CDK, GitLab CI/CD. Kniit: MCP service, Expert Interface on Azure.
